classification.difficultyReason: Students combine straight-angle and triangle sums, then reverse the isosceles property to infer equal opposite sides; part b also requires moving between the whole triangle and a smaller triangle.

content.prompt: Find the values of the pronumerals in these diagrams, giving reasons.

spec.description: Triangle ABC with apex angle 102 degrees and both base angles alpha. Decorative source blue replaced with black.
spec.mathematics: Two equal base angles; angle sum 180 degrees.

spec.description: AB and AC have single equal-side ticks; AM divides the apex into two 18-degree angles. Alpha is at C; beta is below AM at M. No right-angle marker is added.
spec.mathematics: AB=AC; angle BAM=angle MAC=18 degrees; M lies on BC.
spec.answerVisibility: No derived angle or perpendicularity is supplied.

answer.worked:
$AB=AC$, so the base angles at $B$ and $C$ are equal.
$$\begin{align*}\angle BAC&=18^\circ+18^\circ\\\angle BAC&=36^\circ\\2\alpha+36^\circ&=180^\circ\\\alpha&=72^\circ\end{align*}$$
Using the angle sum of $\triangle AMC$:
$$\begin{align*}\beta+18^\circ+72^\circ&=180^\circ\\\beta&=90^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: AB is x, AC is 7; apex angle is 130 degrees, C is alpha, and a curved leader identifies the interior 25-degree angle at B. No units are supplied.
spec.mathematics: Angle A=130 degrees; angle B=25 degrees; AB=x; AC=7.
spec.answerVisibility: Unknown side and angle remain symbolic.

answer.worked:
Triangle angle sum:
$$\begin{align*}\alpha+130^\circ+25^\circ&=180^\circ\\\alpha&=25^\circ\end{align*}$$
The angles at $B$ and $C$ are equal, so their opposite sides are equal: $AB=AC$. Hence $x=7$.

spec.description: Right triangle PQR with QR extended left towards M, PQ labelled x, QR labelled 17, alpha at P and 45 degrees at R.
spec.mathematics: Angle Q=90 degrees; angle R=45 degrees; QR=17.
spec.answerVisibility: No derived equal-side marks or answers are visible.

answer.worked:
Triangle angle sum:
$$\begin{align*}\alpha+90^\circ+45^\circ&=180^\circ\\\alpha&=45^\circ\end{align*}$$
The angles at $P$ and $R$ are equal, so $PQ=QR$. Hence $x=17$.

spec.description: Triangle ABC with A upper left, B lower left and C right; right-angle marker at B, AB=y, BC=11, 45 degrees at A and beta at C.
spec.mathematics: Angle B=90 degrees; angle A=45 degrees; BC=11.

answer.worked:
Triangle angle sum:
$$\begin{align*}\beta+90^\circ+45^\circ&=180^\circ\\\beta&=45^\circ\end{align*}$$
The angles at $A$ and $C$ are equal, so $AB=BC$. Hence $y=11$.

spec.description: Triangle LMN with extended horizontal base, both interior base angles alpha, exterior beta at M, exterior 120 degrees at N, gamma at L, LM=15, LN=x and MN=y.
spec.mathematics: Equal base angles; exterior angle N=120 degrees; LM=15.

answer.worked:
Straight angles at $N$ and $M$:
$$\begin{align*}\alpha+120^\circ&=180^\circ\\\alpha&=60^\circ\\\beta+60^\circ&=180^\circ\\\beta&=120^\circ\end{align*}$$
Triangle angle sum:
$$\begin{align*}\gamma+60^\circ+60^\circ&=180^\circ\\\gamma&=60^\circ\end{align*}$$
All three angles are equal, so their opposite sides are equal. Thus $x=y=15$.
